metadata.title: [BUG]: Admin Users Cannot See Their Own Private Agents in List View
metadata.author: rakdutta

description:
Discovered during: TC-A2A-005 testing (Private Agent Visibility) of issue #2406 

  Test Result: FAILED - Test 2 (Owner can see their own private agent)
  Tests Passed: 7/8

  Symptom

  Admin user with is_admin=true and token_teams=null:
  - ✅ Can create a private agent (201)
  - ✅ Can access their private agent via direct GET /a2a/{agent_id} (200)
  - ❌ Cannot see their private agent in list view GET /a2a (empty result)

  Root Cause

  File: mcpgateway/main.py, lines 4411-4413 in list_a2a_agents() endpoint

  if is_admin and token_teams is None:
      user_email = None  # <-- BUG: This breaks owner matching
      token_teams = None  # Admin unrestricted

  When admin bypass is triggered, the code sets user_email = None to indicate "unrestricted" access. However, this breaks the PR #4341 invariant implemented in mcpgateway/services/base_service.py _apply_access_control() method (lines 109-115):

  if token_teams is None and user_email and is_user_admin(db, user_email):
      return query.where(
          or_(
              model_cls.visibility != "private",
              and_(model_cls.visibility == "private", model_cls.owner_email == user_email),
          )
      )

  This filter requires user_email to be set to match model_cls.owner_email == user_email and show the admin's OWN private agents. When user_email = None, the code falls through to lines 107-108 which exclude ALL private agents:

  if user_email is None and token_teams is None:
      return query.where(model_cls.visibility != "private")

  Expected Behavior (per PR #4341)

  Admin bypass should show:
  - ✅ All public agents
  - ✅ All team agents
  - ✅ Admin's OWN private agents
  - ❌ Other users' private agents (security invariant)
  
  Actual Behavior

  Admin bypass shows:
  - ✅ All public agents
  - ✅ All team agents
  - ❌ NO private agents (including admin's own)
  
  Proposed Fix

  File: mcpgateway/main.py, line 4412

  Remove user_email = None assignment. The token_teams = None is sufficient to trigger admin bypass in _apply_access_control(), and keeping user_email allows the owner matching to work correctly.

  if is_admin and token_teams is None:
      # user_email stays set for owner matching on private agents (PR #4341)
      token_teams = None  # Admin unrestricted - sees all public+team agents

  Impact

  - Admin users cannot see their own private agents in list views
  - Direct GET access still works (uses different code path via _check_agent_access())
  - Affects all resources using the BaseService visibility filtering pattern (agents, potentially others)

  Test Evidence

  ==========================================
  Test 2: Owner can see their own private agent
  ==========================================

  ❌ Test 2 FAILED - Owner cannot see their own private agent
